stem: Water has a much higher specific heat than most other molecules of similar size. Which explanation best accounts for this property?
criteria: A. Much of the heat added to water is used to break hydrogen bonds between water molecules before the molecules can move faster.
B. The covalent bonds inside each water molecule must break before the temperature of the water can rise.
C. Water evaporates easily, and evaporation carries heat away before the water can warm up.
D. Liquid water is dense, so heat is trapped between tightly packed molecules.

stem: An uncharged substance X is at 5 mM outside a cell and 20 mM inside it. Over the next hour, the concentration of X inside the cell rises to 30 mM while the concentration outside stays at 5 mM. Which conclusion is best supported by these data?
criteria: A. X entered by passive transport, because it moved into the cell.
B. X entered by active transport, because it moved from lower to higher concentration.
C. X entered by passive transport, because the membrane is selectively permeable to X.
D. No conclusion is possible without knowing whether a membrane protein carried X.

stem: An enzyme speeds up the conversion of its substrate to product. Which statement correctly describes how the enzyme increases the reaction rate?
criteria: A. It supplies the energy needed for the reaction to occur.
B. It raises the temperature of the solution so that molecules collide more often.
C. It binds any molecule of similar size, so it can speed up many different reactions.
D. It binds the substrate in an active site with a complementary shape, which lowers the activation energy.

A population of beetles lives on tree bark that darkened over several decades. Birds find light-colored beetles more easily than dark-colored ones on the dark bark, and beetle color is heritable. Which outcome is most likely over many generations?
criteria: A. Individual light beetles darken their color to avoid being eaten.
B. The frequency of alleles for dark color increases in the population.
C. The population stays the same because color does not affect reproduction.
D. Birds evolve to see dark beetles more easily within one generation.
